title: Find the Two Swapped BST Values
src: Media.net OA, IIT Guwahati (from a candidate's note), question 2. The note said the tree is given by its root; the mock gives it in LeetCode's level-order form.
body:
A binary search tree with distinct values had the values of exactly two of its nodes swapped, so it is no longer a valid BST.

The tree is given in level order, the way LeetCode serialises trees: -1 stands for a missing child, and missing children of missing nodes are not listed. Return the two swapped values, smaller first.

Function to complete

Complete findSwapped(nodes). It returns the two swapped values, smaller first.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: First line: L, the length of the list. Second line: the L level-order entries (-1 = no node).
out: The two swapped values in increasing order, separated by a space.
cons: Exactly two values are out of place

spec.returns: the two swapped values, smaller first

wrong.why: assumes the swapped nodes are neighbours in sorted order (uses only the first inversion)
treats the level order as if it were the in-order sequence

samples.ex: Root 1, left child 3, whose right child is 2. In-order reads 3 2 1; swapping 1 and 3 gives 1 2 3.

if __name__ == "__main__":
    _raw = sys.stdin.read(); _t = _raw.split(); _p = 0
    _l = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    nodes = list(map(int, _t[_p:_p + (_l)])); _p += (_l)
    _r = Solution().findSwapped(nodes)
    print(" ".join(map(str, _r)))
